correctness.rationale: With the given degree inner product and π=d_w/(2m), exact transfer up to phase preserves energy moments. Hs=−√π e_w and (e_w,Pe_w)_d=0 force γ=1−π by the first moment. The squared target image then gives R_w=||Pe_w||²=d_w/(2m−d_w). Cauchy–Schwarz bounds R_w below by d_w divided by the sum of degrees of the neighbors; this is at least d_w/(2m−d_w). Equality forces equal neighbor degrees and no nonneighbor because all degrees are positive. Conversely a universal apex with k-regular base has π=1/(k+2), and the span of its unit vertex state and the normalized constant on the base is invariant even when the base is disconnected. At the forced γ the two-state block squares to I/(k+2) and maps s to −e_w/√(k+2); its exact exponential gives all stated perfect times and the probability law. This includes k=0 and a two-vertex graph. The cone over P3 has R_w=4/9>3/7 for the apex, so universality alone fails. Independently written exact quadratic-field block checks for 0≤k≤12 and the P3 cone check are replayable with python3 /workspace/branches/9909a74a-ffc2-4579-b873-50462f33f873/independent_check.py. The frozen checker was inspected but not executed: its degree census is rational, its block checks floating point; neither is the all-graph proof.

evidence: The constant-entrance theorem holds for finite irreducible reversible chains with weights and loops and gives a closed-form probability law. Mograby et al. work with the same probabilistic Hamiltonian but their inspected theorem gives approximate bounds. Razzoli et al. prove a universal-marked-vertex result for the combinatorial Laplacian and ordinary uniform input.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The Markov-chain result strictly contains the graph case. The Razzoli theorem does not: the apex of a cone over P3 is a sharp counterexample in the degree-normalized model.
